newsitem.title: USA: Union Pacific calls on Pennzoil shareholders.
newsitem.headline: Union Pacific calls on Pennzoil shareholders.

text.p: Union Pacific Resources Group Inc on Wednesday appealed to Pennzoil Co shareholders to accept its hostile cash and stock offer for the company.
In a letter, the company said that investors should accept its $84 per share bid and "reject a decade of broken promises and poor performance at Pennzoil".
UPR said that its offer is receiving "enthusiastic" support, but needed more shareholders to demonstrate their acceptance.
UPR also questioned how Pennzoil planned to improve the value of its shares to match the $84 offer and what specific forecasts and investment plans supported a value in excess of the bid.

It noted that in 1995 a change in accounting for impaired oil and gas assets, Pennzoil had taken a charge of $379 million, or 10 percent of the book value for its oil, gas and plant, when others on average took a 1.0 percent write down.
"Why were Pennzoil's oil and gas properties so disproportinately impaired? Doesn't this suggest that its investment program has not been successful," UPR said.

The company also questioned whether Pennzoil had the finances to fund its domestic and international exploration and production programmes, noting that Pennzoil had sold stakes in some of its most highly leveraged fields, in the Gulf of Mexico and in Azerbaijan.
Pennzoil sold half of its stake in the Azeri-Chirag-Gunashli block earlier this year for $130 million, leaving it with a 4.8 percent stake in Caspian Sea project.

Union Pacific also demanded to know how Pennzoil's involvement in the Karabakh offshore field in the Caspian would be funded, given the lack of pipeline capacity and the capital needed to fund the project.
No one at Pennzoil was immediately available to comment on UPR's letter. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
